analysis.title: Coffee Break: The voting war
key_insights: Polls point to a clear Democratic win in the House in the 3 Nov 2026 midterms. Control of the Senate (35 of 100 seats up) is an open question.
The largest near-term uncertainty is the Trump administration questioning the legitimacy of the results, which could bring a period of political tension and instability.
Since World War II the president's party has lost an average of 25 House seats and 3.5 Senate seats in midterm elections. The most likely outcome is a political stalemate.
If Democrats win only the House, the administration loses the ability to pass legislation, since most bills need both chambers.
A Democratic Senate would still lack a 60-vote supermajority and a veto-proof majority. Trump has said he will become 'Mr. Veto' if he loses.
UniCredit expects Trump to lean further on executive powers, possibly toward an 'emergency presidency'.
Election lawsuits have almost tripled since 2000. 2020 was the first year above 400 cases, and 2023-2024 was 14.3% above 2019-2020.
The DOJ has filed a pre-election request in California to block counting of some mail-in votes. It has also sued Alaska seeking an injunction against certification if the Republican candidate loses.
Baseline view: Democrats win the House and have a good chance of a narrow Senate majority. Midterms historically have limited market implications.

Any challenge to the results could fuel a temporary 'sell America' trade until certification is complete. UniCredit expects the tension to be short-lived because the president has no power over elections.

tension_points.bull_case: Checks and balances held over the last 18 months. The Trump administration's lawsuits have had a very low success rate. The president has no power over elections, so tensions should be short-lived.
tension_points.bear_case: The administration could cast doubt on the results, bar mail-in ballots, seize voting machines or have states refuse certification. That could fuel a temporary 'sell America' trade.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Challenges persisting beyond the conclusion of the election certification processes.
